# Chih-Yu Lin

::: {.hero-subtitle}
Ph.D. Candidate, National Taiwan University<br>
Visiting Researcher, University of Oulu
:::

## Research vision

Future wireless networks will not only deliver bits. They will support sensing, inference, control, and decision-making under strict timeliness and resource constraints. My research asks three connected questions: *what* information a task needs, *when* that information should be refreshed, and *how* limited wireless resources should be shared. See [Research](research.qmd) for project details.

## Research focus

I develop **learning-based resource allocation** methods for next-generation wireless systems, with an emphasis on information freshness, reliability, and efficient use of radio, sensing, computing, and energy resources. My work spans terrestrial NOMA networks, LEO satellite communications, vehicular ISAC/ISCC, and cooperative multi-RSU sensing.

## Background

Before my Ph.D., I worked as an engineer at TSMC and ASMedia, on semiconductor design workflows and high-speed USB4 IP solutions. This industry experience shapes how I approach wireless systems research: with attention to implementation constraints, not only theoretical performance.
